newsitem.title: USA: Conn. voters approve of US Sen Dodd by 2 to 1-poll.
newsitem.headline: Conn. voters approve of US Sen Dodd by 2 to 1-poll.

text.p: Connecticut voters approve of how U.S. Sen. Christopher Dodd does his job by 62 percent to 27 percent and would re-elect him by about the same margin in a race against former Rep. Gary Franks, a poll said.

While Dodd's approval is up sharply from the 54 percent to 30 percent level a late February poll found, he still trails Sen. Joseph Lieberman, who enjoyed a 72 percent to 14 percent rating, Quinnipiac College said on Tuesday.

Connecticut voters approve more strongly of both senators than they do of their Republican governor, John Rowland, whose approval rating stood at 46 to 23 percent. One of the state officials to capture some of the highest rankings was Attorney General Richard Blumenthal, who was approved of by a 63 to four percent margin, the poll said.

It added that Republican voters had mixed feelings about whether Franks should challenge Dodd in 1998, as 41 percent were in favor, but 37 percent would like another GOP nominee and 22 percent were undecided.

"Despite the fund-raising controversies surrounding the Democratic Party, where Dodd served as general chairman, most residents approve of the way he is doing his job and would vote to re-elect him in a matchup against former Rep. Gary Franks," said Douglas Schwartz, Quinnipiac College Poll Director, in prepared remarks.
The poll of 782 Connecticut residents, who said they were registered voters, was conducted from July 8 to 13, and has a margin of error of plus or minus 3.5 percent.
